nl.title: Website down na update WordPress?
nl.excerpt: WordPress down/critical error: plugins isoleren via File Manager, PHP checken, cache legen.
nl.bodyHtml:
Bij “Website down na update WordPress” isoleer je eerst plugins/thema via bestanden als wp-admin niet opent.

Voorbereiding

  • Backup
  • DirectAdmin File Manager of SFTP

Stappen

  1. Noteer de fouttekst (critical error / 500 / witte pagina).
  2. Via File Manager: hernoem wp-content/plugins naar plugins-off.
  3. Werkt de site: hernoem terug en activeer plugins één voor één tot de boosdoener duidelijk is.
  4. Thema-probleem: activeer een default thema via bestanden of database.
  5. Controleer DirectAdmin → PHP Version Select bij fatals na een update.
  6. Leeg alle caches en test wp-admin + homepage.

Controleren

  • Homepage en wp-admin laden
  • Geen PHP fatals in error_log

Tip: Update niet opnieuw voordat de boosdoener geïsoleerd is.

Let op: Wis geen uploads of database tijdens ‘opschonen’.

Kom je er niet uit? Open een ticket bij TripleZero iT via het klantenpanel. Vermeld je domeinnaam, wat je al hebt geprobeerd en eventuele foutmeldingen (tekst of screenshot).

Gerelateerd: PHP-versie, Installatron-backup.

en.title: Website down after update WordPress?
en.excerpt: Website down after update WordPress: steps in WordPress (wp-admin) for website, down, after.
en.bodyHtml:
For Website down after update WordPress follow a targeted checklist in WordPress (wp-admin). Core themes: website, down, after.

Preparation

  • Access to WordPress (wp-admin)
  • Focus of this article: website, down, after
  • Recent backup or snapshot

Steps

  1. Sign in to WordPress (wp-admin). Filter or search for parts that belong to website, down, after.
  2. Take a backup (Installatron or panel) before changing website.
  3. Sign in to /wp-admin and open Plugins, Themes, Settings, Media or WooCommerce — whatever fits down.
  4. Apply the change; on a critical error isolate via File Manager (rename plugins).
  5. Clear caches and test the pages that touch after.
  6. Document what you changed around website, down, after (old → new value) for support.

Verify

  • Result for website, down, after matches “Website down after update WordPress”
  • No regression on a critical flow beside website down after
  • External test or second browser/network confirms the result

Tip: Work in small steps: get website, down, after right first, then optional extras.

Note: Do not blindly change production without a backup if website, down, after touches login, DNS, mail or payments.

Still stuck? Open a ticket with TripleZero iT via the client panel. Include your domain name, what you already tried, and any exact error messages (text or screenshot).

Related: WordPress (wp-admin), backups, tickets.
